answer: Agent economies fail quietly when identity is free to mint. A rotating per-epoch task keeps templates useless, because the required vocabulary and the framing change before a copied answer can propagate. Think of it as a juniper the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single terrace of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a gale of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. Cost per identity is the whole lever; everything else is decoration.
